title: Buying Property in Türkiye as a Foreigner 2026: Step-by-Step Guide
seoTitle: Buying Property in Türkiye as a Foreigner 2026
metaDescription: Citizens of 183 countries can buy property in Türkiye without a residence permit under Land Registry Law No.
quickAnswer: Citizens of 183 countries can buy property in Türkiye without a residence permit under Land Registry Law No. 2644, subject to military-zone bans and a 30-hectare cap. The 2026 workflow runs from tax number and SPK valuation to DAB currency conversion and TAPU signing, with closing costs led by the 4% title deed fee.
category: Real Estate, Investment, Citizenship & Relocation (ITO Advisory)

body.text: Which nationalities can buy property in Türkiye and what military-zone restrictions exist?

Under Article 35 of Land Registry Law No. 2644, nationals of 183 countries may buy real estate in Türkiye without reciprocity, while select nationalities—including Syrian citizens—remain restricted. Foreign individuals cannot buy inside military or security zones, cannot exceed 30 hectares nationwide, and cannot exceed 10% of any district's private land.

As confirmed by the [Directorate General of Population and Citizenship Affairs (NVI)](https://www.nvi.gov.tr/sss-vatandaslik-hizmetleri) and [Ministry of Foreign Affairs guidance](https://doha-emb.mfa.gov.tr/Mission/ShowInfoNote/207266), foreign buyers do not need a prior Turkish residence permit to hold title ([Invest in Türkiye](https://www.invest.gov.tr/en/investmentguide/pages/acquiring-property-and-citizenship.aspx)). However, specific border provinces, coastal security parcels, and certain nationalities carry additional statutory conditions. A licensed Turkish attorney must verify parcel eligibility directly at the local Land Registry Directorate (Tapu Müdürlüğü) before any deposit changes hands.
What are the exact steps from tax number and SPK appraisal to TAPU title deed?

Official ownership transfers occur exclusively at the Land Registry Directorate ([TKGM](https://www.tkgm.gov.tr/)), never through developer contracts alone. The mandatory 2026 sequence moves from obtaining a Turkish tax number and bank account, ordering an SPK-licensed valuation report, securing a Foreign Exchange Purchase Certificate (DAB), and issuing DASK insurance before TAPU signing with a sworn interpreter.

items: Tax Number & Legal Due Diligence: Obtain a Turkish tax ID (Vergi Kimlik Numarası) and have an independent Turkish attorney inspect the TAPU registry for mortgages, liens, zoning compliance, and İskan (habitation certificate).

SPK-Licensed Valuation Report: Commission a market valuation from a Capital Markets Board (SPK)-authorized appraisal firm connected to TADEBİS, updated under September 2026 rules ([Pera Property 2026 Update](https://www.peraproperty.com/tr/turkey-changes-citizenship-property-valuation-rules-in-september-2026_60064/)).

Foreign Exchange Purchase Certificate (DAB): Convert the foreign-currency purchase price into Turkish Lira through a Turkish bank to the Central Bank (TCMB) and obtain the official DAB ([Legal 500 Türkiye 2026](https://www.legal500.com/intelligence/turkey/real-estate-and-construction/real-estate-investment-in-t%C3%BCrkiye-2026)).

Compulsory Earthquake Insurance (DASK): Purchase an active one-year [DASK](https://www.dask.gov.tr/en/faq) policy in the buyer's name—mandatory for all residential TAPU transfers and utility connections.
TAPU Appointment & Transfer: Attend the TKGM signing (in person with a certified translator or via apostilled Power of Attorney) to pay statutory fees and receive the official title deed.

body.text: What closing costs (4% title deed fee, DASK, notary, lawyer) apply in 2026?

Statutory closing costs in 2026 center on the 4% title deed tax (tapu harcı) on the declared sale price—legally split 2% buyer and 2% seller, though buyers often cover all 4%. Additional mandatory costs include the TKGM revolving fund fee, SPK appraisal, DASK insurance, sworn translation, notary charges, and independent legal fees.

body.text: Why should buyers use an independent advisor and lawyer rather than a developer's agent?

Developer sales agents and commission-paid brokers are financially incentivized to close specific inventory, not to flag missing İskan occupancy permits, inflated appraisal gaps, or restrictive HOA terms. Engaging an independent local advisor for neighborhood scouting alongside a licensed Turkish real estate attorney separates property discovery from legal protection.

faq.q: Do I need a Turkish residence permit before buying property in Türkiye?
faq.a: No. Foreign natural persons can purchase eligible real estate in Türkiye without holding a prior residence permit, using a valid passport and Turkish tax number.

faq.q: Does buying any property in Türkiye automatically grant a residence permit in 2026?
faq.a: No. Under 2026 enforcement of Law No. 6458, qualifying for a residential real estate residence permit (Taşınmaz İkamet İzni) generally requires a standalone residential property valued and declared at USD 200,000 or more outside closed demographic zones.

faq.q: Can I complete a Turkish TAPU transfer without being physically present?
faq.a: Yes. You can grant a specific Power of Attorney to a licensed Turkish attorney either at a Turkish notary public or at a Turkish consulate / apostilled notary abroad, translated and certified into Turkish.

faq.q: What is an İskan certificate and why does it matter?
faq.a: An İskan (Yapı Kullanma İzin Belgesi) is the municipal habitation license confirming a building was constructed in compliance with its approved architectural project. Buying without it can complicate utility subscriptions and future resale.

faq.q: Are foreign buyers exempt from Turkish VAT (KDV) on new-build properties?
faq.a: Non-resident foreign buyers purchasing a brand-new property directly from a developer may qualify for VAT exemption if payment arrives in foreign currency from abroad and the property is held for the statutory period—verify exact eligibility with a licensed Turkish tax attorney.
